AS A RESULT OF THE COVID-19 VIRUS, AND RESULTING ORDERS AND DIRECTION FROM THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES, THE GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, AND THE ORANGE COUNTY HEALTH CARE AGENCY, AS WELL AS THE CITY OF IRVINE EMERGENCY DECLARATION, THE PUBLIC WILL NOT BE PERMITTED TO PHYSICALLY ATTEND THE IRVINE CITY COUNCIL MEETING TO WHICH THIS AGENDA APPLIES.
YOU MAY SUBMIT COMMENTS ON ANY AGENDA ITEM OR ON ANY ITEM NOT ON THE AGENDA, IN WRITING VIA MAIL TO “ATTN: CITY COUNCIL,” ONE CIVIC CENTER PLAZA, IRVINE, CA 92606; BY EMAIL TO CLERK@CITYOFIRVINE.ORG; OR THROUGH E-COMMENT AT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV. YOU MAY WATCH THE MEETING LIVE ON ICTV, COX COMMUNICATIONS LOCAL ACCESS CHANNEL 30, AND AT&T U-VERSE CHANNEL 99, AND LIVESTREAMED ONLINE AT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV.
PLEASE NOTE: THE CITY COUNCIL IS MAKING EVERY EFFORT TO FOLLOW THE SPIRIT AND INTENT OF THE BROWN ACT AND OTHER APPLICABLE LAWS REGULATING THE CONDUCT OF PUBLIC MEETINGS, IN ORDER TO MAXIMIZE TRANSPARENCY AND PUBLIC ACCESS. IT WOULD BE APPRECIATED IF COMMUNICATIONS OF PUBLIC COMMENTS RELATED TO ITEMS ON THE AGENDA, OR ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA, ARE PROVIDED PRIOR TO THE COMMENCEMENT OF THE MEETING. IF THAT IS NOT POSSIBLE, EVERY EFFORT WILL BE MADE TO ATTEMPT TO REVIEW E-COMMENTS DURING THE COURSE OF THE MEETING. TOWARDS THIS END, THE MAYOR WILL ENDEAVOR TO TAKE A BRIEF PAUSE BEFORE ACTION IS TAKEN ON ANY AGENDA ITEM TO ALLOW THE CITY CLERK TO REVIEW E-COMMENTS, AND SHARE ANY E-COMMENTS RECEIVED DURING THE MEETING.

NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council and Successor Agency meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council and/or Successor Agency meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council/Successor Agency meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv. For more information, please contact the City Clerk's office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council/Successor Agency will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council/Successor Agency meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council/Successor Agency meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council/Successor Agency meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council/Successor Agency regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk's Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council/Successor Agency Board.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE

MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  AND
  REGULAR JOINT MEETING
  WITH THE CITY OF IRVINE AS
  SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE
  DISSOLVED IRVINE
  REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY

  July 28, 2020
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER
The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council and regular joint meeting with the City of Irvine
as Successor Agency to the dissolved Irvine Redevelopment Agency was called to order at
5:32 p.m. on July 28, 2020, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic
Center Plaza, Irvine, California; Mayor/Chairwoman Shea presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present:  5  Councilmember/Boardmember:  Melissa Fox
  Councilmember/Boardmember:  Farrah N. Khan
  Councilmember/Boardmember:  Anthony Kuo
  Mayor Pro Tempore/Vice Chairman:  Mike Carroll
  Mayor/Chairwoman:  Christina Shea

Mayor/Chairwoman Shea announced that the meeting was broadcast live on Cox
Communications Local Access Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse Channel 99, and
livestreamed online at cityofirvine.org; and that in an effort to protect public health and
prevent the spread of COVID-19, the e-comment feature had been extended for all agenda
items, which allowed members of the public the ability to submit e-comments through the
 City Council Minutes  July 28, 2020

  public comment portion of each item and would be included as part of the official record and
  uploaded to the City’s website. She also assured the community that the City of Irvine was
  adhering to the Governor’s Executive Order in the Council Chamber and throughout City Hall
  by sanitizing surfaces and equipment, as well as wearing face masks.

  Mayor/Chairwoman Shea also announced that general public comments for the City Council
  on items not on the agenda would be considered at approximately 6:30 p.m., which had been
  standard practice prior to the COVID-19 pandemic, and expressed her appreciation for
  everyone’s patience and understanding as the City continued to make adjustments to
  meeting protocols as needed.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Mayor/Chairwoman Shea led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Pastor Mike Anderson from Good Shepherd Lutheran Church in Irvine provided the
  invocation.

  1.  CITY COUNCIL RECOGNITIONS

  1.1  Commend the United Across Borders Foundation on its June 27,
  2020, Food Distribution Event

  Mayor Shea presented a commendation to the United Across Borders
  Foundation for its June 27, 2020, food distribution event at the Orange
  County Great Park, which resulted in over 1,300 cars being filled with fresh
  fruits, vegetables, and groceries that greatly benefitted those in need during
  this difficult time; and expressed her appreciation to Councilmembers Fox
  and Khan for bringing the item forward.

  Councilmember Fox also expressed her appreciation to the United Across
  Borders Foundation for its collaborative efforts and generosity to those in
  need.

  Molly Perry, City Clerk, noted that an e-comment was received by
  Anonymous Resident, who suggested that the commendation speak more
  to the efforts made by the United Across Borders Foundation.

  CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  There was no report.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  July 28, 2020

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  •  Councilmember Khan, as the City’s representative to the Orange County Mosquito
  and Vector Control District (OCMVCD), announced that OCMVCD had confirmed the
  first mosquito samples infected with West Nile virus in the City of Irvine, and
  encouraged residents to take steps to protect themselves by applying EPA-registered
  repellent, wearing long-sleeved clothing, and eliminating potential breeding sources
  around properties, such as standing water. For information on West Nile virus, visit
  ocvector.org.

  •  Councilmember Fox expressed concern about the public’s inability to provide verbal
  testimony at City Council meetings, and suggested that live testimony be permissible
  via Zoom or other type of digital platform. In addition, Councilmember Kuo noted that
  some members of the public expressed concern about potential non-compliance with
  the Ralph M. Brown Act (Brown Act), to which City Attorney Melching provided a brief
  summary of the Governor’s Order related to temporary waivers of the Brown Act
  during the pandemic, and assured the City Council that it was in compliance with those
  requirements.

  Mayor Shea made the following announcements:

  •  The application period for the Rental Assistance Program closed on Friday, July 24,
  with 1,877 applications received. Residents had the option of applying for one of two
  grants, which included a maximum one-time $1,000 grant for assistance with lease
  termination fees, or a maximum one-time $1,000 grant for rental payment assistance.
  Staff are diligently reviewing applications for eligibility. Grants will be distributed in the
  coming weeks as funding becomes available to the City via the federal CARES Act.

  •  A variety of summer camps will be offered for children and teens to have fun and learn
  new skills in a safe environment that meets State and County health guidelines. Camp
  options include music, theater, reading, science, baking, LEGO, and more. There will
  also be additional options for kids at Irvine park sites. The goal is to keep children and
  staff safe while providing much needed summer fun. Activities are structured to
  maintain social distancing, and camp supplies are never shared between children. For
  information on new camps added each week, visit yourirvine.org each Monday.

  •  In an effort to provide family fun while following safety guidelines, the Orange County
  Great Park will host the “Summer Drive-In Series” beginning August 1 through August
  29. The series has been well received by the public so far, with all tickets reserved by
  residents within the first 48 hours.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  July 28, 2020

  •  The City of Irvine and the American Red Cross are hosting a blood drive on
  Wednesday, August 12 at the Orange County Great Park in the Artist Studios at the
  Palm Court Arts Complex. There is a constant need for blood, which can potentially
  save up to three lives and help ensure patients do not have to wait to receive needed
  care. To schedule an appointment, visit redcrossblood.org and use sponsor code:
  cityofirvine.

  •  The third week of the COVID-19 drive-up testing program is underway at the Orange
  County Great Park. To date, 2,055 individuals have been tested, and capacity was
  expanded to allow additional testing in the second week. Approximately 1,200 people
  will be tested this week. Test results are available in two to three days after the
  appointment. The City of Irvine was the first city in Orange County to provide COVID-
  19 testing to those who live or work in Irvine, regardless of whether symptoms are
  shown. The no-cost PCR testing is available by appointment only and takes place
  Mondays through Thursdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

  ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS

  There were no additions or deletions to the agenda.

  ASSOCIATION DONATION

  Molly Perry, City Clerk, noted that the following e-comments had been

  •  Chelsea Boyle, who spoke in opposition to the acceptance of the
  donation, and spoke in favor of defunding the police.

  •  Anonymous Resident, who expressed appreciation to South Coast
  Chinese Cultural Association for its support of the Public Safety
  Department and City’s mission.

  Mayor Shea reiterated that the donation was made for the purposes of
  repairing Public Safety vehicles that sustained damage while assisting with
  mutual aid during recent protests in a neighboring city; and both Mayor
  Shea and Councilmember Fox expressed their appreciation to the South
  Coast Chinese Cultural Association for its generosity.

  Councilmember Kuo inquired about a potential conflict-of-interest given that
  he currently serves as an unpaid trustee of the South Coast Chinese
  Cultural Association, to which City Attorney Melching confirmed that no
  conflict-of-interest existed.
